title: ZrSiX: butterfly magnetoresistance from Fermi-surface geometry

decision_points.fork: Chemical potential: electron counting (12 of 24 spinless bands filled) vs the E_FERMI of the archived WannierTools inputs
decision_points.consequence: mu off by 10.5 and 35.6 meV; compensation broken (n_e/n_h 0.68, 1.90); MR(B||b) saturates (exponent 0.26 vs 1.60), butterfly peak moves to 46.8 deg, sample ratio 1.65 vs 2.25

decision_points.fork: ZrSiS input.dat is a copy of the ZrSiSe file (Se atoms, ZrSiSe cell, same E_FERMI)
decision_points.wrong_choice: Take the ZrSiS chemical potential from its input.dat
decision_points.consequence: mu(ZrSiS) 0.78 eV below the neutral point (a pure hole metal)

decision_points.fork: Electron count and spin counting of the spinless 24-orbital model (24 valence electrons; NumOccupied = 13 in the ZrSiTe input)
decision_points.wrong_choice: 13 filled bands for ZrSiTe, or carrier density without the spin factor 2
decision_points.consequence: mu(ZrSiTe) 0.97 eV too high; densities low by a factor 2

decision_points.fork: k-mesh convergence of the Chambers integral (40/80/160 meshes)
decision_points.consequence: 40 mesh fakes saturation for B||b (exponent 0.27), puts the peak at 35.6 deg and MR(b)/MR(c) = 0.93; 80 mesh gives MR(b)/MR(c) = 2.15 (-18%)

decision_points.fork: Origin of the angular pattern: Chambers on the real Fermi surface vs a closed-orbit effective-mass (two-band Drude) model
decision_points.consequence: Monotonic angular dependence with the maximum at an end point (90 deg) instead of 54.8 deg

decision_points.fork: Kohler scaling: compare samples at their own B*tau (5 and 2 T ps), not at equal B*tau
decision_points.wrong_choice: Compare both at B*tau = 5 T ps (or swap)

graded_fields: neutral_mu_eV for ZrSiS, ZrSiSe, ZrSiTe (+-3 meV)

length_estimate.why: Neutral points by counting (6 cheap calls), then dense-mesh transport at 3 units each: the agent cannot buy the full 160-mesh angle scan (24 directions = 72 units) plus the ZrSiTe and convergence checks, so it must choose which directions and meshes to buy.

runtime_dependencies: numpy, scipy-free numpy evaluators (runtime image); lab data 11 MB of npz lookups, no extra image layer

zrsite_mr_c_over_b.tolerance: +-25% (guards against mesh 40; mesh 80 is caught by mr_b_over_c)

notes: Graded values come from the lab evaluator on the archived Hamiltonians (no archived MR curves exist in the record). The 160 mesh was checked against a 240 x 240 x 120 run for the graded ZrSiSe/ZrSiTe directions; all 240 values lie inside the windows. Hall-resistivity sign changes are not graded: for the compensated crystals rho_yx is not converged even at 160/240. ZrSiTe band 14 and the unsymmetrized-model asymmetry change the graded values by <2% and are rubric items only.
